clinician.trajectory_summary: A 47-year-old female with established mixed connective tissue disease (2018) and psoriatic arthropathy (2020) underwent routine screening mammography demonstrating incidentally discovered bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy without suspicious breast findings. Targeted bilateral breast and axillary ultrasound revealed numerous enlarged lymph nodes (largest 30×5mm) with Doppler findings of intra- and extranodal vascularization favoring an active inflammatory process. The inflammatory etiology was subsequently confirmed, and the patient was advised to continue regularly scheduled mammographic screening without requiring invasive biopsy, consistent with reactive lymphadenopathy secondary to underlying autoimmune disease.
